editorialHook: The fog is doing its moody November thing, the holiday lights are starting to flicker on, and somehow SF has packed one of its best weeks of the year into seven little days.

picks.d: Sammy's personal pick of the week, full stop. The British R&B soul queen brings her stunning voice to the Castro Theatre, one of the most beautiful rooms in the city. If you can get a ticket, you will be talking about this one for years.

Six nights, six different themes, one of indie rock's greatest storytellers holding court at the Fillmore. John Darnielle and company are doing something genuinely rare here, and each night is its own distinct experience. Grab any night you can.

Ten years of a debut album that genuinely changed how people think about neo-soul and conscious hip-hop, and Jamila Woods is celebrating it right here at the Rickshaw Stop. Tickets are $35 advance and $40 day of show, so grab them now. This is an intimate room for a giant talent.

picks.t: Bhangra and Beats Diwali Night Market
picks.d: A free, festive outdoor market at Yerba Buena Gardens blending South Asian culture, music, food, and dancing at one of SoMa's best outdoor spaces. This is the kind of only-in-SF evening that reminds you why you live here. Zero dollars, maximum vibes.

picks.t: Tank and The Bangas - The Last Balloon Tour
picks.d: New Orleans neo-soul and funk royalty, led by the magnetic Tarriona Tank Ball, hit August Hall to kick off your Friday right. With support from Ariel J. and DJ Zeus, this is a full evening of genre-blending goodness that will have you moving from the first note. One of the most purely fun shows of the week.

One of the biggest names in dark, hypnotic techno lands at SF's premier dance destination for what will almost certainly be a sweaty, transcendent Saturday night. Deborah De Luca is internationally celebrated for a reason, and Halcyon is the perfect room for it. Clear your Sunday morning.

picks.t: ZENEFIT 2026 - A Night of Sonic Exploration
picks.d: A one-of-a-kind benefit evening at Great American Music Hall featuring a DJ set from the eclectic Devendra Banhart, plus born i and more. Tickets run $40 to $160 and the whole thing is designed around deep, immersive listening. Equal parts art event, music night, and community gathering.

picks.t: Performing Arts Showcase at Fulton Plaza
picks.d: Fulton Plaza lights up under the SPECTRA holiday lights for a free showcase bringing together some of SF's most exciting performing arts organizations. It is a perfect no-cost kickoff to the weekend with serious wow factor. Bundle it with the Diwali Night Market and you have a full free Friday evening.

picks.t: Dear San Francisco - Home for the Holidays
picks.d: The critically acclaimed immersive circus experience at Club Fugazi is back with its holiday edition, running through December 30. Acrobatics, aerial work, music, and storytelling all wrapped in a love letter to the city itself. Opening week is the perfect time to catch it fresh.

Your favorite winter tradition kicks off tonight: immersive art and science of light, luminous artworks, optical illusions, and that unmistakable Exploratorium energy, but for adults only. This is opening night of Glow, which means the energy is at a peak. Grab tickets in advance, they go fast.

Juno Award-winning Canadian singer-songwriter Allison Russell brings her soul-stirring blend of folk, gospel, and Americana to one of the great rooms in rock history. Her live shows are known for being emotionally powerful and visually captivating. A quieter pick this week but an absolute gem.

Detroit legend Sherard Ingram, aka DJ Stingray, is one of the most anticipated DJ bookings of the month in SF. He came up alongside the original Detroit techno innovators and his masked electro-techno sets are blistering, singular experiences. Tickets are $15 to $25 and this is a room you will not want to leave.

The 27th annual SF VegFest returns to the SMC Event Center with speakers, vegan chefs, and a full day of plant-based celebration for $18. Whether you are fully vegan or just veg-curious, this is a fun, food-forward way to spend a Saturday afternoon. Bring your appetite and your tote bag.

picks.t: Golden Gate Bandshell - Tribute to Legends
picks.d: Four free hours of live music celebrating musical legends in the heart of Golden Gate Park. Pack a blanket, grab a coffee, and settle in for one of the best free mornings the city has to offer. No tickets, no cover, no catch.

ongoing.t: SFMOMA - RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me
ongoing.d: BTS leader RM's personal collection of Korean modernists alongside SFMOMA's own holdings - a genuinely surprising and beautiful show.

ongoing.t: de Young - Treasures of the Pharaohs
ongoing.d: On view through January 31, 2027 - Bay Area residents get free general admission on Saturdays with a Bay Area ID.

ongoing.t: Asian Art Museum - Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean
ongoing.d: Southeast Asia's largest ancient bronze is making a once-in-a-lifetime stop in San Francisco through January 25.

ongoing.t: ACT - John Proctor Is the Villain
ongoing.d: West Coast premiere of Kimberly Belflower's explosive coming-of-age story, running through December 6 at the Toni Rembe Theater.

ongoing.t: Peter Pan Goes Wrong - SF Playhouse
ongoing.d: A chaotic comedy of backstage disasters that will have you doubled over in laughter, running through November 28.
From the team behind experiences for Billie Eilish and the Las Vegas Sphere, showing until November 29.

new.name: Oklava
new.d: The team behind Turquaz just opened this Mediterranean-inspired spot inside the Saluhall food hall - a fresh and exciting addition to the corridor.

new.name: Rize Up Cafe
new.d: Azikiwee Anderson's beloved sourdough brand now has its own cafe, with cheddar and kimchi grilled cheese and smoked trout tartines built on those iconic loaves.

new.name: Bayview Oyster Bar
new.d: Grilled and raw oysters, clam chowder, and Dungeness crab with garlic noodles anchor this exciting new seafood spot at 5114 3rd St.

new.name: Bar Antoine Lounge
new.d: A stylish new mezzanine bar in the Galleria Park Hotel with serious fine-dining pedigree and inventive bites like the Dim Saumon salmon mousse.

new.name: Ah Ma's Kitchen
new.d: Landing at No. 16 on Yelp's Best New Restaurants of 2026 list, this Cantonese-inspired spot on Clement Street is a must-visit for the Richmond.

new.name: Rose Pizzeria
new.d: One of SF's most beloved 2026 openings, with a 10/10 sourdough tang rating and a house pizza wine at $13 a glass.

classic.name: Chicano Nuevo
classic.d: Six courses of masa worship with an average check of $190 for two - the most exciting splurge in the city right now.

classic.name: Fat Cat and The Mantis
classic.d: Called 2026's most fun dinner spot by The Infatuation, this natural-wine-forward Bernal Heights gem is creative, lively, and genuinely joyful.

classic.name: Bare Bones
classic.d: Three restaurant pros opened this counter-service spot on Taraval built around slow-cooked rotisserie chicken that is crowd-pleasing perfection.

classic.name: Ruay Mitr Chicken and Rice
classic.d: New fast-casual Thai from the operator behind Saam and Song Wat, carving out a sharp niche in focused, affordable Thai dining.

bars.name: Bar Antoine Lounge
bars.d: New mezzanine bar above Le Parc Bistro Bar with a French-leaning cocktail list and bites like the bamboo-steamed Dim Saumon.

bars.type: Natural Wine Bar / Late Night - Mission
bars.name: Bar Part Time
bars.d: The Mission's beloved natural wine bar known for late-night dance raves and a crowd that genuinely loves both wine and dancing.

bars.name: Dalva
bars.d: A Mission classic with a killer back bar, and a partner venue to the upcoming Downtime - the kind of neighborhood bar you stay at way too late.

bars.name: Halcyon
bars.d: SF's premier intimate dance club with a tight-knit house music community and marathon dance nights - Deborah De Luca plays here Saturday.

bars.name: Underground SF
bars.d: A 100-cap Lower Haight staple at 424 Haight St known for dark, serious dance floor energy with no frills and all music.

bars.name: The Great Northern
bars.d: One of SF's top underground spots with a warehouse aesthetic and world-class sound system - Frequency 8 lands here Saturday night.

bars.name: 1015 Folsom
bars.d: SF's big-room dance institution with Eli and Fur Friday night and Detroit legend DJ Stingray closing out the week on Thursday.

bars.name: Audio Nightclub
bars.d: Nora En Pure plays a rare 2pm to 7pm day party here Saturday - her organic progressive house sound is a perfect fit for this room.

games.detail: Away game at Smoothie King Center, New Orleans
Away game at American Airlines Center, Dallas

sports.note: No Warriors home games this week. Next home game is Nov 22 vs Boston Celtics at Chase Center.

games.detail: Franklin Square, The Mission - recreational league with strong post-game social scene

sports.note: Great way to meet active people - register at volosports.com.

concerts.d: Deep electronic sounds at one of SF's best-regarded electronic music clubs. A solid, immersive way to kick off the weekend for fans who like their Friday nights dark and hypnotic.
An emerging OnesToWatch artist in an intimate small-room setting at the beloved Cafe Du Nord. This is the kind of show you will brag about catching before they blew up - window favors early buyers.

A Bay Area folk-pop favorite known for introspective songwriting and warm stripped-back performances. The Independent's intimate setting is perfect for a close-and-personal Saturday show with a beloved local.
Romanian pop superstar with infectious dance-pop anthems and a massive international fanbase brings her high-energy show to August Hall's stylish room. A proper Saturday night pop party.

A beloved Bay Area indie folk act in one of the city's most storied rooms. At $30 advance and $35 day of show, this is an intimate evening with a genuinely singular songwriter in a room that suits her perfectly.
concerts.venue: Great American Music Hall - $30 ADV / $35 DOS

concerts.d: Alt-country legends Son Volt paired with Texas country icon Kelly Willis is as good a double bill as Americana fans are going to find this month. Jay Farrar's literate roots-rock songwriting deserves a room this good.

concerts.t: Computerwife with Double Helix Peace Treaty
concerts.d: A quirky, indie and experimental closer at the beloved 4 Star Theater. If you like your Thursday nights a little left-of-center with great support acts, this is your move to close out the week.
A free weekly reggae-themed concert in the heart of Golden Gate Park for a laid-back Sunday evening. No cover, all vibes, and the kind of only-in-SF free experience that never gets old.
concerts.venue: Golden Gate Bandshell, Golden Gate Park - FREE

concertsOngoing.t: The Mountain Goats Residency at the Fillmore
concertsOngoing.d: Six nights, six themes, running November 15 through 21 - grab any available night for one of indie rock's most beloved storytelling acts.

concertsOngoing.t: Golden Gate Bandshell Friday Happy Hour
concertsOngoing.d: Every Friday 4:30 to 7:30 PM in Golden Gate Park - free live music to wind down the work week, no tickets needed.

singles.t: SF Social Club - Full Hearts Full Plates Friendsgiving
singles.d: A warm, cozy potluck social at ERIA Marina on Chestnut Street designed to help you relax and connect with new people in the community. Thanksgiving energy without the family chaos - honestly kind of ideal. Members only, so check the SF Social Club site to join.

The British melodic house duo in a great room with tickets starting at $4.37 - yes, really - making this one of the best value nights out this week. The dance floor at 1015 is legitimately one of the better places to meet fellow music lovers in SF. 21 plus.

singles.t: Bontan, Jordan Michael and Santino at Halcyon
singles.d: Deep house and tech house until 4am at SF's most community-driven dance club, with $12 tickets before 11pm. Halcyon has a genuinely tight-knit regular crowd and a friendly vibe that makes it easier than most clubs to actually talk to people. 21 plus.

singles.t: Nora En Pure Day Party at Audio
singles.d: A Saturday afternoon progressive house show is a genuinely great format for meeting people - relaxed, early enough to grab dinner after, and anchored by one of the most beloved DJs in the organic house world. Tickets start at $55, so this is a crowd that is there on purpose. 21 plus.

singles.t: Founders Running Club at Murphy Windmill
singles.d: A free weekly run in Golden Gate Park with a brainy, sociable crowd of founders, investors, operators, and creative people. Easy 5 to 10km pace means you can actually hold a conversation, and the post-run coffee chat is where the real connecting happens.

singles.t: Volo Sports Coed Soccer at Franklin Square
singles.d: Recreational coed 8v8 soccer in the Mission with Volo Sports, the city's go-to league for people who want to play sports and also make friends who are not from work. Teams welcome solo sign-ups, so no crew needed to show up.

singlesOngoing.d: Tuesday nights in Golden Gate Park, Thursday speedwork at Kezar Stadium, and Saturday adventure runs - all free and all genuinely social.
Recurring structured speed dating at The Jay Hotel - meet 8 to 12 local singles in one efficient, low-pressure evening.

date.title: Golden Gate Park Golden Hour
date.tagline: Four hours of free music, fresh air, and zero pressure.

steps.title: Tribute to Legends Concert
steps.detail: Pack a blanket and head to the Golden Gate Bandshell for the free four-hour concert celebrating musical legends. Find a good spot, share a coffee from a thermos, and let the music do the talking.

steps.title: Walk Through the Park
steps.detail: After the show winds down, wander through Golden Gate Park together - Stow Lake, the Conservatory of Flowers, or just wherever looks interesting.

steps.title: Crucial Reggae Sunday
steps.detail: Circle back to the Bandshell for Crucial Reggae Sunday, running 4:30 to 7:30 PM. Still free, still outdoors, and the vibe shifts to something more laid-back and evening-ready. Perfect.

date.title: Diwali Night Market to Neo-Soul Night
date.tagline: Street food, dancing, and a show that will give you chills.

steps.title: Bhangra and Beats Diwali Night Market
steps.detail: Start the evening at Yerba Buena Gardens for the free Diwali Night Market. Eat whatever smells best, watch the dancers, and soak up the energy of one of SF's most festive free events.

steps.title: Dinner at Rose Pizzeria
steps.detail: Head to 1 Clement Street in the Richmond for some of the city's best sourdough pizza and a glass of the house pizza wine at $13. Relaxed, delicious, and totally unpretentious.

steps.title: Jamila Woods at the Rickshaw Stop
steps.detail: Make it to the Rickshaw Stop by 8pm for Jamila Woods celebrating 10 Years of HEAVN. Tickets are $35 advance and this is an intimate room for a massive talent - an evening you will both remember.

date.title: Castro Theatre and a Big Night Out
date.tagline: An unforgettable room, an unforgettable voice.

steps.title: Drinks at Bar Antoine Lounge
steps.detail: Start at the new mezzanine bar in the Galleria Park Hotel. Order the Dim Saumon and a French-leaning cocktail from Christie Chemel's list. It is intimate, stylish, and sets a great tone.

steps.title: Dinner at Fat Cat and The Mantis
steps.detail: Head to Bernal Heights for what The Infatuation called 2026's most fun dinner spot. Natural wine, creative food, and a lively room that feels like a great dinner party.

steps.title: Jorja Smith at the Castro Theatre
steps.detail: Monday November 16 - Jorja Smith in one of the most beautiful rooms in San Francisco. Her voice in that space is something you simply cannot replicate anywhere else. Book now.

solo.title: Free SF Friday
solo.tagline: An entire evening of only-in-SF experiences that cost absolutely nothing.

steps.title: Performing Arts Showcase at Fulton Plaza
steps.detail: Walk over to Civic Center for the free holiday showcase under the SPECTRA lights. SF's most exciting performing arts orgs, all in one outdoor space. Just show up.

steps.title: Stroll to Bhangra and Beats Diwali Night Market
steps.detail: It is a quick trip from Civic Center to Yerba Buena Gardens where the Diwali Night Market runs until 9pm. Eat, wander, listen to music, feel alive.

steps.title: Wrap up and decompress
steps.detail: Walk home through SoMa or hop on transit. You just had a full, beautiful Friday evening and spent nothing. That is the city working the way it is supposed to.

solo.title: Museum Afternoon Plus Thao
solo.tagline: A quietly perfect solo Sunday in the city.

steps.title: de Young Museum - Treasures of the Pharaohs
steps.detail: Bay Area residents get free general admission on Saturdays with a Bay Area ID, so this is a nearly free museum afternoon. The Pharaohs show requires a timed ticket but is worth it. Take your time.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Walk
steps.detail: After the museum, wander the park at your own pace. The Conservatory of Flowers, the buffalo paddock, or just wherever your feet take you. This is the good stuff.

steps.title: Thao at Great American Music Hall
steps.detail: Doors at 7pm, show at 8pm, $30 advance tickets. GAMH is one of the great rooms in SF and Thao is a beloved Bay Area voice. A solo show at a great venue is a genuinely restorative experience.

solo.title: Glow Night at the Exploratorium
solo.tagline: A sensory evening built for curiosity and wonder.

steps.title: Dinner at Rize Up Cafe
steps.detail: Head to SoMa for a early dinner at Rize Up Cafe. The cheddar and kimchi grilled cheese on that legendary sourdough is a perfect pre-event meal. Quick, delicious, and very SF.

steps.title: Exploratorium After Dark - Glow Opening Night
steps.detail: This is opening night of the Glow installation, 21 plus, running 6 to 10pm. Luminous artworks, optical illusions, and the full Exploratorium experience for adults. Buy tickets in advance - they sell out.

steps.title: THROTTLE - DJ Stingray at 1015 Folsom
steps.detail: Walk or cab from the Exploratorium to 1015 Folsom. Detroit legend DJ Stingray goes until 2am and tickets are $15 to $25. The ideal way to extend a great evening into a genuinely legendary night.

birthday.title: Golden Gate Park Birthday Hang
birthday.tagline: Your birthday, the park, and free music. Classic.

steps.title: Tribute to Legends Concert
steps.detail: Tell everyone to meet at the Golden Gate Bandshell with blankets and snacks. Four hours of free live music is the most chill birthday morning you can organize with zero effort.

steps.title: Park Picnic
steps.detail: After the concert, find a good spot in the park and stretch the afternoon out. Someone brings a cake. Everyone brings something. This is the move.

steps.title: Crucial Reggae Sunday to close
steps.detail: End the afternoon back at the Bandshell for Crucial Reggae Sunday, free until 7:30pm. The birthday crew winds down with great music and no bill to split. Perfection.

birthday.title: Mission Night Out for the Birthday Crew
birthday.tagline: Dinner, dancing, and the best neighborhood in the city.

steps.title: Dinner at Chicano Nuevo
steps.detail: Six courses of masa worship in the Mission at $95 per person with the tamale add-on. Reserve well in advance. This is a tasting menu experience that will anchor the whole evening as a genuine memory.

steps.title: Drinks at Bar Part Time
steps.detail: The Mission's natural wine bar and late-night dance haven is right in the neighborhood. Great wine, low pretension, and a crowd that actually knows how to have fun. Birthday energy is very welcome here.

steps.title: Dance at Halcyon or 1015
steps.detail: Either Deborah De Luca at Halcyon Saturday or Eli and Fur at 1015 on Friday. Pick your night, pick your room, and dance until you have no choice but to go home.

birthday.title: Jorja Smith Birthday Night
birthday.tagline: Make it a night nobody forgets.

steps.title: Pre-show Dinner at Fat Cat and The Mantis
steps.detail: 2026's most fun dinner spot in Bernal Heights for the crew - natural wine, creative food, the kind of lively room that is already a party before the party starts.

steps.title: Jorja Smith at the Castro Theatre
steps.detail: Monday November 16. Book the tickets now, gather your people, and walk into one of the most beautiful venues in America to hear one of the best voices in music. Birthday show of the year.

steps.title: After drinks in the Castro
steps.detail: The Castro neighborhood has great late-night bar options right outside the Theatre. Extend the evening in one of SF's most iconic neighborhoods. The birthday person should not pay for a single drink.

friends.title: Diwali Night Market and Bandshell
friends.tagline: A full free Friday evening that actually impresses the crew.

steps.title: Golden Gate Bandshell Friday Happy Hour
steps.detail: Meet at the Bandshell in Golden Gate Park for the free Happy Hour series running 4:30 to 7:30 PM. Bring drinks in a bag if that is your style. No tickets, no cover.

steps.title: Head to Yerba Buena for Diwali Night Market
steps.detail: The Bhangra and Beats Diwali Night Market runs until 9pm at Yerba Buena Gardens. Eat street food, watch performers, and wander around with no agenda. A free, festive group hang.

steps.title: Decide what comes next
steps.detail: The night is young and you have spent nothing. Underground SF is a few blocks away with a $0 door situation earlier in the evening, or just find a bar in SoMa. The crew energy takes it from here.

friends.title: VegFest Saturday then Nora En Pure
friends.tagline: A full Saturday of food and music that works for every kind of friend.

steps.title: SF VegFest 2026
steps.detail: The 27th annual VegFest at the SMC Event Center is $18 and runs 11am to 5pm. Speakers, chefs, samples, and a lot of fun even if nobody in the group is fully vegan. Bring your appetite.

steps.title: Lunch inside VegFest
steps.detail: Eat your way through the vendor stalls. This is the main event inside the main event. Budget $15 to $25 for food and you will eat very well.

steps.title: Nora En Pure Day Party at Audio Nightclub
steps.detail: The progressive house day party runs 2 to 7 PM at Audio with tickets from $55. The timing is perfect for a group that just came from VegFest and wants to transition into full Saturday mode.

friends.title: Dear San Francisco Opening Week
friends.tagline: An immersive circus night the whole group will talk about for months.

steps.title: Pre-show drinks at Bar Antoine Lounge
steps.detail: Meet at the new Galleria Park Hotel mezzanine bar for French cocktails and the Dim Saumon bites before heading across town. It is a stylish pre-show ritual.

steps.title: Dinner at Ah Ma's Kitchen on Clement
steps.detail: Head to the Richmond for Cantonese-inspired dishes at Yelp's No. 16 Best New Restaurant of 2026. Family-style dishes are made for groups and the whole Clement Street corridor is festive right now.

steps.title: Dear San Francisco - Home for the Holidays at Club Fugazi
steps.detail: Opening week of the holiday edition of this acclaimed immersive circus show at 678 Green St in North Beach. Tickets from $86.90. Acrobatics, aerial work, music, and storytelling - a full experience that works for every type in the group.

parents.title: Saturday in the Park with the Folks
parents.tagline: A morning of free live music and Golden Gate Park at its best.

steps.title: Tribute to Legends Concert
steps.detail: The Golden Gate Bandshell free concert runs 10am to 2pm on Saturday. Blankets, coffee from a nearby cafe, and four hours of live music celebrating musical legends. Zero effort, maximum enjoyment for every generation.

steps.title: Lunch on Irving or 9th Avenue
steps.detail: Walk a few blocks from the park to the Inner Sunset for lunch. Lots of relaxed, affordable options with minimal wait and a neighborhood feel that tends to be a hit with visiting parents.

steps.title: de Young Museum - Treasures of the Pharaohs
steps.detail: Walk back into the park to the de Young. Bay Area residents get free general admission on Saturdays with a Bay Area ID, so only the Pharaohs special exhibition requires a ticket. A museum this good is a gift.

parents.title: Allison Russell and a Fillmore Night
parents.tagline: Take your parents to the Fillmore. It never fails.

steps.title: Asian Art Museum - Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean
steps.detail: A once-in-a-lifetime ancient bronze from Southeast Asia at Civic Center is a genuinely awe-inspiring way to start the day with parents who appreciate culture. The Ha Chong-Hyun retrospective is also on view.

steps.title: Lunch at Rose Pizzeria in the Richmond
steps.detail: One of SF's most beloved new openings, with a relaxed atmosphere and 10/10 sourdough pizza. The house wine at $13 a glass makes this a very easy lunch to sell to any parent.

steps.title: Allison Russell at the Fillmore
steps.detail: A Juno Award-winning folk and gospel songwriter at one of the most famous music venues in America. The Fillmore experience - the posters, the room, the balcony - impresses parents every single time. Saturday November 14.

parents.title: John Proctor, Dinner, and the Castro
parents.tagline: Theater, great food, and a neighborhood walk that shows off the city.

steps.title: SFMOMA - RM x SFMOMA and Graciela Iturbide
steps.detail: Start the day at SFMOMA with two incredible shows - the RM Korean modernist collection and five decades of Graciela Iturbide photography. Jacob Hashimoto's Giant Arc installation on the first floor is free.

steps.title: Lunch near Union Square
steps.detail: Bar Antoine Lounge in the Galleria Park Hotel is a stylish and interesting lunch option with French-leaning bites and cocktails, right in the Union Square area. Parents tend to love a good hotel bar lunch.

steps.title: John Proctor Is the Villain at ACT
steps.detail: The West Coast premiere of this critically acclaimed show runs through December 6 at the Toni Rembe Theater. Tickets from $35 and the production quality is at the highest level. A genuinely memorable evening of theater.
